SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p821/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p821/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p821/r2.claim: The singular form is used for divine oneness or another context, such as an individual punishment.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p821/r2.anchor: ويستعمل الإفراد إذا كان المقام مقام توحيد أو مقام آخر كالعقوبة المنفردة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r1.claim: Affluent leaders of Makkah and Ṭāʾif mistook wealth for proof that they were God's favorites and expected still more; Muhammad should leave their fate to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r1.anchor: These verses admonish the megalomaniac leaders of Makkah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r2.claim: The wording resembles 73:11, where Muhammad is also told to leave the comfortable rejecters to God for a little respite.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r3.claim: Being created alone means entering life without wealth, status, companions, or confidants; these are God's favors and should inspire gratitude, not entitlement to more in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r3.anchor: when man comes into this world, he is without wealth and status and without comrades and confidants

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r4.claim: The passage describes a general wealthy, high-status mentality, not Walīd ibn Mughīrah alone, though it applies to him too.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r4.anchor: there is no reason for restricting the verse to him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r1.claim: Early scholars' reports that a verse was revealed about a person can mean that person is one application, not the occasion of revelation; the passage diagnoses a common arrogant mentality.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r2.claim: The word used for the person can refer to singular or plural antecedents, fitting the passage's general application.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r2.anchor: used here which is used for both singular and plural entities

RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r1.claim: They unanimously identify the person meant as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r1.anchor: أجمعوا على أن المراد ههنا الوليد بن المغيرة

RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r2.claim: One parse makes waḥīdan an accusative circumstantial expression referring to God: “Leave me alone with him; I suffice to take vengeance on him.”
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r2.anchor: أنه نصب على الحال ، ثم يحتمل أن يكون

RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r3.claim: If the circumstantial expression refers to God, it can mean that God created al-Walīd alone, with no partner in creation.
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r3.anchor: خلقته وحدي لم يشركني في خلقه أحد

RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r4.claim: If it refers to al-Walīd, it means that God created him initially alone, without wealth or children, as in 6:94.
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r4.anchor: وأما كونه حالا من المخلوق ، فعلى معنى أني خلقته حال ما كان وحيدا

RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r5.claim: A second parse treats waḥīdan as an accusative of disparagement: the verse addresses al-Walīd by the boastful nickname al-Waḥīd, which he used for himself and his father.
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r5.anchor: القول الثاني : أنه نصب على الذم

RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r6.speaker: كثير من المتأخرين
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r6.claim: Many later scholars object that this reading would make God affirm al-Walīd’s claim that he was unique and without equal.
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r6.anchor: وطعن كثير من المتأخرين في هذا الوجه

RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r7.claim: Rāzī rejects that objection: al-Waḥīd may be a proper name rather than a quality, just as the condemned person in 44:49 is called “the mighty, the noble.”
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r7.anchor: أنا لما جعلنا الوحيد اسم علم فقد زال السؤال

RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r8.claim: A second reply is that al-Walīd may be called unique only in his own belief, as illustrated by 44:49.
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r8.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يحمل على كونه وحيدا في ظنه واعتقاده

RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r9.claim: A third reply is that “unique” does not specify high rank; al-Walīd is unique only in disbelief, vileness, and lowliness.
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r9.anchor: أن لفظ الوحيد ليس فيه أنه وحيد في العلو والشرف

RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد الضرير
RAZI-FULL:v30p175/r10.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḍarīr parses waḥīdan as the second object of “created” and defines al-waḥīd as one without a father, casting doubt on al-Walīd’s lineage, as in 68:13.

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r1.claim: The passage is commonly believed to target al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, a determined opponent of the Prophet in Mecca.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r1.anchor: These verses are believed to refer to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, a staunch opponent of the Prophet in Makkah

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r2.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates that al-Walīd’s heart softened after hearing the Prophet recite; Abū Jahl pressured him to denounce Muhammad, and al-Walīd praised the Quran’s unlike-poetry, sweet, abundant speech before branding it inherited sorcery, prompting this passage.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r2.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās related that al-Walīd went to the Prophet, who recited the Quran to him, and his heart seemed to soften to it

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r3.claim: One reading takes “alone” as God, emphasizing His uniqueness as Creator.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r3.anchor: Alone refers either to God, thus emphasizing His Uniqueness as Creator

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r4.claim: Alternatively, the human being begins and ends life alone before God.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r4.anchor: or to the human being, who begins and ends life alone before God

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r5.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r5.claim: Al-Waḥīd is also reported as an epithet of al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r5.anchor: which is also said to be one of the epithets by which

TAB-FULL:v23p422/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r1.claim: God tells the Prophet to leave to Him the affair of the man created alone in his mother’s womb, with neither wealth nor child.
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} [المدثر: 11] قال: خلقته وحده ليس معه مال ولا ولد

TAB-FULL:v23p422/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r2.claim: The person singled out is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī.
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: أنزل الله في الوليد بن المغيرة قوله: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا}

TAB-FULL:v23p422/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the verse was revealed concerning al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, along with the passage beginning at 15:92.
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: أنزل الله في الوليد بن المغيرة قوله: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا}

TAB-FULL:v23p422/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r4.claim: Mujāhid explains that the man was created alone, with no wealth or child.
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} [المدثر: 11] قال: خلقته وحده ليس معه مال ولا ولد

TAB-FULL:v23p422/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r5.claim: Mujāhid says it was revealed about al-Walīd, though everyone was created in the same solitary state.
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} [المدثر: 11] قال: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة، وكذلك الخلق كلهم

TAB-FULL:v23p422/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r6.claim: Qatāda identifies al-Walīd, created with nothing, whom God later enriched with wealth, children, abundance, and increase.
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} [المدثر: 11] وهو الوليد بن المغيرة

TAB-FULL:v23p422/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the passage from this verse through the threat of being cast into Saqar was revealed about al-Walīd.
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} [المدثر: 11] إلى قوله

TAB-FULL:v23p422/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r8.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the person meant is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
TAB-FULL:v23p422/r8.anchor: يعني الوليد بن المغيرة {وجعلت له مالا ممدودا}

TABATABAI:74:8-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r1.claim: These verses threaten those who disparage the Qurʾan by calling it magic and mock truths it contains.
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r1.anchor: في الآيات وعيد شديد للطاعنين في القرآن الرامين له بأنه سحر والمستهزئين لبعض ما فيه

TABATABAI:74:8-11/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r9.claim: The verse is a threat; abundant reports say it and the following nineteen verses were revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r9.anchor: كلمة تهديد وقد استفاض النقل أن الآية وما يتلوها إلى تمام عشرين آية نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

TABATABAI:74:8-11/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r10.claim: Best parsing: waḥīdan is a circumstantial accusative of the subject of ‘I created’; God created him alone, then arranged his affairs, so the Prophet should leave him to God.
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r10.anchor: وقوله { وحيدا } حال من فاعل { خلقت } ومحصل المعنى دعني ومن خلقته

TABATABAI:74:8-11/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r11.claim: Another parsing makes waḥīdan a circumstantial accusative of the object of ‘leave me.’
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r11.anchor: ومن المحتمل أن يكون حالا من مفعول { ذرني }

TABATABAI:74:8-11/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r12.claim: A further proposal makes the implied object of ‘I created’ its antecedent: he was created alone, without wealth or sons.
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r12.anchor: وقيل حال من مفعول خلقت المحذوف وهو ضمير عائد إلى الموصول، ومحصل المعنى

TABATABAI:74:8-11/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r13.claim: Another proposal treats waḥīdan as an accusative with an implied ‘I condemn’; the author says the first parsing is best.
TABATABAI:74:8-11/r13.anchor: واحتمل أيضا أن يكون { وحيدا } منصوبا بتقدير " أذم " وأحسن الوجوه أولها

TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r3.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r3.claim: Al-Qummi says the verses about the solitary man concern al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: moved by the Prophet’s recitation, he was pressured by Abu Jahl to call it sorcery, and the verse was revealed.
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r3.anchor: فإنها نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة وكان شيخا كبيرا مجربا من دهاة العرب

TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r4.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r4.claim: Al-Walid was called ‘solitary’ because he claimed to handle the Kaaba’s covering alone one year and Quraysh collectively the next; he had ten sons and great wealth.
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r4.anchor: وإنما سمي وحيدا لأنه قال لقريش أنا أتوحد لكسوة البيت سنة وعليكم في جماعتكم سنة

TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r5.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r5.claim: The report says each of al-Walid’s ten slaves traded with a thousand dinars; qintar then could mean a bullhide filled with gold.
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r5.anchor: وكان له عشرة عبيد عند كل عبد الف دينار يتجر بها وتلك القنطار في ذلك الزمان

TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas’s report, transmitted by Ikrima and cited by al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi, says al-Walid softened after hearing Qur’an; Abu Jahl suggested Quraysh would pay him because they thought he sought money. Al-Hakim authenticated it.
TABATABAI:74:8-31#2/r6.anchor: أخرج الحاكم وصححه والبيهقي في الدلائل من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس أن الوليد بن المغيرة جاء إلى النبي

TABATABAI:74:8-31#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:74:8-31#3/r1.claim: The continuation of Ibn Abbas’s report says al-Walid praised Qur’an as sweet, radiant, fruitful, and unsurpassed, then called it transmitted sorcery after pondering; the verse was revealed.
TABATABAI:74:8-31#3/r1.anchor: قال قد علمت قريش أني من أكثرها مالا. قال فقل فيه قولا يبلغ قومك أنك منكر

TABATABAI:74:8-31#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31#3/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله وأبو جعفر
TABATABAI:74:8-31#3/r2.claim: Al-Ayyashi reports from Zurara, Humran, and Muhammad ibn Muslim that Abu Abd Allah and Abu Ja‘far said al-wahid means a child born outside marriage.
TABATABAI:74:8-31#3/r2.anchor: روى العياشي بإسناده عن زرارة وحمران ومحمد بن مسلم عن أبي عبد الله وأبي جعفر عليهما السلام أن الوحيد ولد الزنا

TABATABAI:74:8-31#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:8-31#3/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:74:8-31#3/r3.claim: Zurara recounts Abu Ja‘far’s reply to a Hashimite who called himself ‘son of the solitary one’: the term means someone whose father is unknown.
TABATABAI:74:8-31#3/r3.anchor: قال زرارة ذكر لأبي جعفر عليه السلام عن أحد بني هشام أنه قال في خطبته أنا ابن الوحيد

BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r2.claim: Wāḥidan can be circumstantial of the speaker—“leave me alone with him”—or of God—“I created him alone.”
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r2.anchor: حال إما من الياء أي ذرني وحدي معه

BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r3.claim: With an omitted object pronoun, the phrase means the one created alone, originally without wealth or children; the verse was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r3.anchor: أي ومن خلقته وحيدا فريدا لا مال له ولا ولد نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r4.claim: God mockingly turns al-Walīd’s title al-Waḥīd against him: he is isolated in wealthlessness or lineage as an illegitimate claimant, or uniquely evil and base.
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r4.anchor: فسماه الله بالوحيد تهكما به واستهزاء بلقبه

BURSEVI:v10p176/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p176/r1.claim: The Najmī allusion makes al-Walīd the solitary evil soul; his wealth, bad traits, followers, and prestige symbolize sins and the dark natural powers of a rebellious self.
BURSEVI:v10p176/r1.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : يشير إلى الوليد بن مغيرة

BURSEVI:v10p176/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p176/r2.claim: Abū Bakr the hidden, ʿUmar the spirit, ʿUthmān the secret, and ʿAlī the heart use spiritual light to erase the self’s darkness, defeat its deeds and followers, and end its dominion.
BURSEVI:v10p176/r2.anchor: يعني دعني وإياه فإني أسلط عليه أبا بكر الخفي وعمر الروح وعثمان السر وعلى القلب

TABRISI:74:11-31/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:11-31/r3.claim: God tells Muhammad to leave the described unbeliever to Him, for God will punish him; the phrase is an idiom meaning “leave me and him.”
TABRISI:74:11-31/r3.anchor: أي دعني وإياه فإني كاف له في عقابه كما يقول القائل دعني

TABRISI:74:11-31/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:11-31/r4.claim: If waḥīdan describes the created man, it means he was created alone in his mother’s womb, without wealth or children; the man is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
TABRISI:74:11-31/r4.anchor: وإن حملته على صفة المخلوق فمعناه دعني ومن خلقته في بطن أمه واحد

TABRISI:74:11-31/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31/r5.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:74:11-31/r5.claim: Muqatil glosses the command as “leave him between Me and him,” since God will destroy him alone.
TABRISI:74:11-31/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: معناه خل بيني وبينه فأنا أفرد بهلكته

TABRISI:74:11-31/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:74:11-31/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says al-Walid was known as “the Unique One” among his people.
TABRISI:74:11-31/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كان الوليد يسمى الوحيد في قومه

TABRISI:74:11-31/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:74:11-31/r7.claim: A report from al-ʿAyyashi says Abu Jaʿfar explained al-waḥīd as a child of unknown paternity; boasting “son of the unique one” would therefore be shameful.

THALABI:v10p70/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p70/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p70/r4.claim: God created him alone in his mother's womb, without wealth or children; the verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi.
THALABI:v10p70/r4.anchor: ذرني ومن خلقت أي خلقته في بطن أمه وحيدا فريدا لا مال له ولا ولد. نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي.

THALABI:v10p70/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p70/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p70/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-Walid was called al-Wahid, the unique one, among his people.
THALABI:v10p70/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس وكان يسمى: الوحيد في قومه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi refers back to his explanation at “Leave Me with the deniers.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r1.anchor: ذكرنا معنى هذا عند قوله: {وذرني والمكذبين}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r2.claim: Muqatil says God tells Muhammad to leave the man between God and himself, for God will destroy him alone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني: خل يا محمد بيني وبينه، فأنا أنفرد بهلكته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r3.claim: The relative pronoun has an omitted object understood as “whom I created.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r3.anchor: والعائد إلى الموصول محذوف على تقدير: خلقته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r4.claim: The commentators agree that these verses were revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r4.anchor: وأجمعوا على أن هذه الآيات نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r5.speaker: أكثر المفسرين وأهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r5.claim: The dominant explanation is that God created al-Walid alone in his mother’s womb, with no wealth, children, or wife; on this reading, “alone” describes the created man.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r5.anchor: خلقته وحده لا مال له، ولا ولد، ولا زوجة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r6.speaker: الفراء والكسائي والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r6.claim: They offer another construction in which “alone” describes God: He created the man without any partner in creation, so He knows him and has power over him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r6.anchor: وهو: أن يكون الوحيد من صفة الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r7.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r7.claim: ʿAta reports that al-Walid called himself “the unique son of the unique,” claiming no Arab or father was his equal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r7.anchor: قال: يريد الوليد بن المغيرة، وكان يقول: أنا الوحيد بن الوحيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi rejects this as the meaning of “I created him alone”: God would not affirm al-Walid’s boast that he had no equal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p415#2/r8.anchor: وهذا غير صحيح أنه لا يجوز أن يكون تفسيرا لقوله: "خلقت وحيدا"

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r1.claim: Muhammad need not worry about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra; God will handle him. He was created alone, without wealth or children.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r1.anchor: { ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا } أي: لا تهتم لشأنه فإني أكفيك أمره، أي: الوليد بن المغيرة، يقول: خلقته وحيدا لا ولد له

ELMALILI:74:5-12/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r13.claim: Wahidan can be a circumstantial phrase for the Creator, uniquely creating without a partner, or for the created person, made solitary and unsupported.
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r13.anchor: mahluk olan تَمْنُن’den de hâl olabilir. Yani Benimle bırak

ELMALILI:74:5-12/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r14.claim: The image of being created alone applies to every individual, as in the verse that people will come singly as first created.
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r14.anchor: her ferd hakkında sahihtir. Ve bununla kıyametin de hilkat gibi bilhassa ferdî safhasına işaret buyurulmuş demektir

ELMALILI:74:5-12/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r15.claim: The verse points to an individual phase of resurrection, just as creation began with each person alone.
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r15.anchor: kıyametin de hilkat gibi bilhassa ferdî safhasına işaret buyurulmuş demektir

ELMALILI:74:5-12/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r16.claim: The occasion of revelation is reported to have been al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi.
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r16.anchor: Bunun sebeb-i nüzûlü Velîd b. Mugīre el-Mahzûmî olduğu rivayet olunuyor

ELMALILI:74:5-12/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r17.claim: Although the occasion is specific, the warning applies generally according to the traits described.
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r17.anchor: Sebeb-i nüzûlün has olması hüküm ve inzârın vasıflara nazaran umûmî olmasına mâni‘de değildir

ELMALILI:74:5-12/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r18.claim: Some say the wording hints that al-Walid was a foundling or illegitimate claimant, as discussed in Surat Nun, and was called Wahid.
ELMALILI:74:5-12/r18.anchor: Sûre-i Nûn’da geçtiği vechile zenîm, da‘iyy olduğuna îmâ

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r1.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r1.claim: Exegetes report that these verses were revealed about the Meccan polytheist al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r1.anchor: Müfessirler bu âyetlerin Mekkeli müşrik Velîd b. Mug^re hakkında indiğini rivayet etmişlerdir (Taberî, XXIX, 96; Şevkânî, V, 376).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r2.claim: Al-Walīd was a wealthy Quraysh notable with many sons, yet instead of thanking God for His gifts he was ungrateful to God and the Prophet and led efforts to suppress Islam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r2.anchor: Velîd, Kureyş’in ileri gelenlerinden olup çok sayıda oğulları vardı ve oldukça zengindi; buna rağmen Allah’ın kendisine lutfettiği nimetlere şükredecek yerde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r3.claim: One interpretation is: leave to God the person He created helpless and alone in the womb; God will punish him without the Prophet’s involvement.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r3.anchor: Anasının karnında âciz ve tek başına bir durumda yarattığım o şahsı bana bırak, senin onunla uğraşmana gerek yok, ben onun cezasını veririm.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r4.claim: A second interpretation is: leave him alone with God, who will deal with him and inflict the due punishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r4.anchor: Onu tek başına benimle baş başa bırak; ben onun hakkından gelir ve gereken cezayı veririm

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.claim: The passage’s general lesson is that gratitude to the giver of blessings is a basic moral duty grounded in reason and justice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.anchor: Nimete karşı şükretmek, nimet sahibine minnettar olmak en yalın ahlâkî ödevlerden biri, akıl ve adalet gereğidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.claim: Failing to thank God for life and material and spiritual gifts is grave ingratitude, especially when it advances denial, polytheism, and injustice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.anchor: varlığımızı, hayatımızı, sahip olduğumuz, yararlandığımız her türlü maddî ve mânevî nimet ve imkânları lutfeden Allah’a minnettar olmamak, şükretmemek

BURHAN:v4p436/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p436/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
BURHAN:v4p436/r1.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows a conjunctive waw, which the author rejects because it makes God tell the Prophet to leave both Him and the created person; the sense is to leave God alone with them.
BURHAN:v4p436/r1.anchor: أجاز أبو البقاء كون الواو عاطفة وهو فاسد لأنه يلزم فيه إن يكون الله تعالى أمر نبيه

BURHAN:v4p436/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p436/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p436/r2.claim: The intended idiom is “leave me to deal with them,” like leaving a she-camel with her foal to suckle.
BURHAN:v4p436/r2.anchor: فتعين إن يكون المراد خل بيني وبينهم وهو وارد مع كقولك لو تركت الناقة وفصيلها

BURHAN:v2p197/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p197/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p197/r6.claim: وحيدا can describe the one God created alone, solitary and apart from wealth and children.
BURHAN:v2p197/r6.anchor: فإنه يحتمل أن يكون خلقته وحيدا فريدا من ماله وولده

BURHAN:v2p197/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p197/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
BURHAN:v2p197/r7.claim: Al-Baqa allows the conjunction to mean leave Me and the person I created alone, but the author rejects it because it would order the Prophet to leave both him and the deniers; the waw means leave them to Me, as in تركت الناقة وفصيلها.
BURHAN:v2p197/r7.anchor: وهو فاسد لأنه يلزم منه أن يكون الله قد أمر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يتركه

QUSHAYRI:v3p363/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p363/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p363/r18.claim: Do not concern yourself with their affair: God will take care of it, having created the person alone without a partner.
QUSHAYRI:v3p363/r18.anchor: لا تهتم بشأنهم ، ولاتحتفل ؛ فإني أكفيك أمرهم . إني خلقته وحدي ؛ لم يشاركني في خلقي إياه أحد

QUSHAYRI:v3p363/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p363/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p363/r19.claim: Alternatively, the person was created alone without a supporter.
QUSHAYRI:v3p363/r19.anchor: ويحتمل : خلقته وحده لا ناصر له

BURHAN:v1p163/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p163/r1.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v1p163/r1.claim: The unnamed man created alone in the verse is identified as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
BURHAN:v1p163/r1.anchor: وقد قيل فى قوله تعالى ﴿ ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا ﴾ إنه الوليد بن المغيرة

ITQAN:v4p394/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p394/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p394/r2.claim: The person created alone is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
ITQAN:v4p394/r2.anchor: 5758 ﴿ ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا ﴾ هو الوليد بن المغيرة

RUMMANI:v1p88/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p88/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p88/r1.claim: In ذرني, the literal sense is to leave the punishment and stop interceding; the metaphor magnifies the threat although God cannot be restrained, since any punishment He can impose is exceeded by none.
RUMMANI:v1p88/r1.anchor: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} ذرني ها هنا مستعار

DAMGHANI:v1p483/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p483/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p483/r9.claim: Dharanī means leave me alone with the one I created; the source parallels the phrase about the prosperous deniers.
DAMGHANI:v1p483/r9.anchor: فوجه منهما ذرني وكذا يقول خل بيني وبين كذا قوله تعالى في سورة المدثر ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#3/r1.claim: The man was initially alone, with neither wealth nor sons.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#3/r1.anchor: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} أي فردا: لا مال له ولا بنين

NAHHAS:v5p65/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p65/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p65/r17.claim: من is accusative as comitative object or coordinated with the first-person pronoun; وحيدا is circumstantial accusative.
NAHHAS:v5p65/r17.anchor: من في موضع نصب على أنها مفعول معه أو عطف على النون والياء وحيدا نصب على الحال

SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r1.claim: ومن خلقت has the same two syntactic analyses discussed for والمكذبين in the preceding sūra.
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r1.anchor: في الوجهين المتقدمين في السورة قبلها

SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r2.claim: وحيدا may be circumstantial from the speaker's pronoun in ذرني: leave him alone with Me, since I will take revenge on him.
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r2.anchor: أنه حال من الياء في " ذرني " أي: ذرني وحدي معه فأنا أكفيك في الانتقام منه

SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r3.claim: Alternatively, وحيدا may modify the subject of خلقت: God created him alone, without a partner, and therefore owns him.
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r3.anchor: أنه حال من التاء في " خلقت " أي: خلقته وحدي لم يشركني في خلقه أحد

SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r4.claim: Other parses make وحيدا circumstantial from من or from the omitted relative pronoun in the clause.
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r4.anchor: الثالث: أنه حال من " من ". الرابع: أنه حال من عائد المحذوف أي: خلقته وحيدا

SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r5.claim: وحيدا may be accusative of disparagement; if it is Walīd ibn al-Mughīra's established nickname, it must be parsed this way.
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r5.anchor: الخامس: أن ينتصب على الذم. و " وحيد " كان لقبا للوليد بن المغيرة

SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r6.claim: وحيد may mean lowly and insignificant; alternatively, Walīd claimed uniqueness in merit and wealth, but the nickname does not prove it.
SAMIN-DURR:74:11/r6.anchor: ومعنى " وحيدا ": ذليلا قليلا. وقيل: كان يزعم أنه وحيد في فضله وماله

ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r4.claim: Zajjāj refers readers to his earlier explanation of dharnī in Sūrat al-Muzzammil.

ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r5.claim: Waḥīdan is an accusative circumstantial phrase and has two possible referents.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r5.anchor: و (وحيدا) منصوب على الحال، وهو على وجهين:

ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r6.claim: One analysis describes God as alone in creating the man, with no partner sharing in creation.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r6.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون وحيدا من صفة الله - عز وجل - المعنى ذرني

ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r7.claim: Alternatively, waḥīdan describes the created man as having been made alone, without wealth or children.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r7.anchor: ويكون (وحيدا) من صفة المخلوق، ويكون المعنى، ذرني ومن خلقته

ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r10.claim: The passage is said to refer to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who had ten sons and was wealthy.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r10.anchor: وهذا قيل يعنى به الوليد بن المغيرة، كان له بنون عشرة وكان موسرا

ASAD-NOTES:74:11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:11/r1.claim: God says He created the man alone.
ASAD-NOTES:74:11/r1.anchor: him whom I have created alone

ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r1.claim: Wahid can mean either that God alone created the man or that God created the man alone.
ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r1.anchor: The above sentence can be understood in either of these two senses

ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r2.claim: If wahid describes God, it stresses His uniqueness as Creator; if it describes the man, it evokes his utter loneliness at life's beginning and end.
ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r2.anchor: stressing His uniqueness as Creator - or to this particular object of His creation, man, who begins and ends his life in a state of utter loneliness

ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r3.claim: Either reading emphasizes man's inescapable dependence on God.
ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r3.anchor: In either case, our attention is drawn to the fact of man's inescapable dependence on God

ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r4.claim: The phrase also means to leave God alone to decide what to do with one who forgets his Creator and Sustainer, forbidding human punishment of truth-deniers.
ASAD-NOTES:74:11#n5/r4.anchor: Leave it to Me alone to decide what to do with him who forgets that I am his Creator and Sustainer

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.claim: Meccan opponents repeatedly alleged that the Quran was human fabrication, borrowed ancient lore, or material copied from earlier writings and dictated to Muhammad; the Quran records these charges and reasons against their falsehood.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.anchor: ويسجل القرآن مفترياتهم لا يكتمها، ويجادلهم فيها بما يهدي كل ذي عقل وبصيرة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.claim: Al-Muddaththir is the counterpart of the preceding al-Muzzammil; their central themes are essentially the same and their names share a meaning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.anchor: There is no essential difference between the central themes of both sūrahs .

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.claim: Verses 11–17 warn that Judgment Day will be severe for disbelievers who presume their wealth and rank will bring them still more.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.anchor: The Prophet (sws) should well inform the people about the afflictions of the Day of Judgement.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r7.claim: The arrogant man began life alone, without wealth or status, when God created him in his mother's womb.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r7.anchor: they were totally alone in this world; they neither had wealth nor status at that time.

IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.claim: At the pilgrimage season, Quraysh ask al-Walid for a single story about Muhammad; after rejecting soothsayer, madman, poet, and sorcerer as accurate descriptions, he recommends calling him a sorcerer because people see him as dividing families.
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.anchor: ثم إن الوليد بن المغيرة اجتمع إليه نفر من قريش، وكان ذا سن فيهم، وقد حضر الموسم

IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq identifies the subject as al-Walid and explains that he was a contentious adversary.
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r2.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى في الوليد بن المغيرة وفي ذلك من قوله: ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p328#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p328#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p328#2/r1.claim: ʿIkrima relates that al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra was moved by the Prophet's recitation and praised its sweetness and power, but after Abū Jahl pressed him to say something against it, called it transmitted magic; the verse was revealed about him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p328#2/r1.anchor: عن رجل عن عكرمة أن الوليد بن المغيرة جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأ عليه القرآن فكأنه رق له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r1.claim: There is no disagreement that the passage was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r1.anchor: ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا: لا خلاف أنها نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r2.claim: Al-Walīd was reportedly nicknamed “the unique” because none equaled his wealth or family standing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r2.anchor: فروي أنه كان يلقب بالوحيد، أي لأنه لا نظير له في ماله وشرفه في بيته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r3.claim: The apparent parse makes waḥīdan a circumstantial accusative of the omitted pronoun: God created him alone, poor, and childless before granting wealth and sons.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r3.anchor: والظاهر انتصاب وحيدا على الحال من الضمير المحذوف العائد على من، أي خلقته منفردا ذليلا قليلا لا مال له ولا ولد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r4.claim: Mujāhid parses waḥīdan from the pronoun in “leave me”: leave me alone with him to punish him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r4.anchor: وقيل: حال من ضمير النصب في ذرني، قاله مجاهد، أي ذرني وحدي معه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r5.claim: Another parse attaches waḥīdan to the subject of “I created”: God created him without a partner and needs no helper to destroy him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r5.anchor: أو حال من التاء في خلقت، أي خلقته وحدي لم يشركني في خلقي أحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r6.claim: The view that waḥīdan means unknown parentage is problematic as an insult; the author replies that the title is a proper name or means uniquely evil.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r6.anchor: وقيل: وحيدا لا يتبين أبوه. وكان الوليد معروفا بأنه دعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r7.claim: The rebuttal is that a nickname no longer states a quality; waḥīdan can mean unique in disbelief, wickedness, and baseness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r7.anchor: ورد ذلك بأنه لما لقب بذلك صار علما، والعلم لا يفيد في المسمى صفة، وأيضا فيمكن حمله على أنه وحيد في الكفر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Walīd b. al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī, according to reports from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatādah, and others; it is even said to be agreed upon.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r1.anchor: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وغيرهم بل قيل كونها فيه متفق عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r2.claim: If the occasion concerns al-Walīd’s later conduct, the sūra cannot all have been revealed at the very beginning of the mission.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r2.anchor: وهو يقتضي أن هذه السورة لم تنزل جملة إذ لم يكن أمر الوليد وما اقتضى نزول الآية فيه في بدء البعثة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid takes “alone” as circumstantial from the first-person object: leave him to Me alone, since God needs no other avenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r3.anchor: وحيدا حال إما من الياء في ذرني وهو المروي عن مجاهد أي ذرني وحدي معه فأنا أغنيك في الانتقام عن كل منتقم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, “alone” is circumstantial from “I created”: God created him without any partner and can destroy him without help.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r4.anchor: أو من التاء في خلقت أي خلقته وحدي لم يشركني في خلقه أحد فأنا أهلكه لا أحتاج إلى ناصر في إهلاكه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers attaching “alone” to the omitted pronoun referring to “whom”: the man began solitary, without property or children.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r5.anchor: أو من الضمير المحذوف العائد على من على ما استظهره أبو حيان أي ومن خلقته وحيدا فريدا لا مال له ولا ولد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r6.claim: It may instead be an object of condemnation: al-Walīd was nicknamed “the Unique,” so the verse mocks his title or turns expected praise into blame, calling him uniquely wicked.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r6.anchor: وجوز أن يكون منصوبا بأذم ونحوه فقد كان الوليد يلقب في قومه بالوحيد فتهكم الله تعالى به وبلقبه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r7.claim: A further gloss is that he was alone in wickedness, or cut off from his presumed father because he was an adopted child of uncertain lineage.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p121#2/r7.anchor: فأراد سبحانه وحيدا في الخبث والشرارة أو وحيدا عن أبيه لأنه كان دعيا لم يعرف نسبه للمغيرة حقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#3/r3.claim: His attractive prosperity earned him the nickname “the fragrance of Quraysh,” and he was called “the Unique” as the one deemed most entitled to leadership.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#3/r3.anchor: يلقب ريحانة قريش وكذا كانوا يلقبونه بالوحيد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p266/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p266/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p266/r8.claim: Wahīdan means God created him alone in his mother's womb, with neither wealth nor children.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p266/r8.anchor: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} أي: خلقته في بطن أمه وحيدا فريدا لا مال له ولا ولد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p266/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p266/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p266/r9.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, known as unique among his people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p266/r9.anchor: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، كان يسمى الوحيد في قومه

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r1.claim: The passage was revealed concerning al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r2.claim: Waḥīdan may be circumstantial from the first-person pronoun: “leave me alone with him,” for God will suffice against him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r2.anchor: حال من الياء أي ذرني وحدي معه فإني أكفيكه

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r3.claim: Alternatively, it is circumstantial from the subject of “I created,” meaning God created him alone, with no partner.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r3.anchor: أو من التاء أي ومن خلقته وحدي لم يشركني في خلقه أحد

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r4.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the omitted object: he was created alone, without wealth or children.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r4.anchor: أو من العائد المحذوف أي من خلقته فريدا لا مال له ولا ولد

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r5.claim: The word may derisively repeat his nickname, or mean he was alone in wickedness or illegitimacy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r5.anchor: أو ذم فإنه كان ملقبا به فسماه الله به تهكما، أو إرادة أنه وحيد ولكن في الشرارة أو عن أبيه فإنه كان زنيما

BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r1.claim: After warning that many will face judgment in disbelief, God consoles the Prophet, who grieves for people hostile to him, and promises to deal with their arrogance and delusion.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r1.anchor: هون أمرهم عليه وحقر شأنهم لديه بوعده بالكفاية بقوله مستأنفا منبها على أسباب الهلاك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r2.claim: God tells the Prophet to leave Him to deal with the man in whatever way the situation requires.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r2.anchor: ذرني } أي أتركني على أي حالة اتفقت

BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r3.claim: The man was created from nothing and formed through stages, originally possessing no wealth, children, or property.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r3.anchor: أوجدت من العدم وأنشأت في أطوار الخلقة , حال كونه { وحيدا * } لا مال له ولا ولد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r4.claim: God alone created the man without a partner and remains firmly one in His oneness; the man failed to thank Him and instead committed shirk.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r4.anchor: وحال كوني أنا واحدا شديد الثبات في صفة الوحدانية لم يشاركني في صنعه أحد

DURR-FULL:v8p327/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p327/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p327/r9.claim: Qatada identifies the man created alone as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, born without wealth or children and later given wealth, offspring, riches, and increase.
DURR-FULL:v8p327/r9.anchor: عن قتادة {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: هو الوليد بن المغيرة أخرجه الله من بطن أمه وحيدا لا مال له ولا ولد فرزقه الله المال والولد والثروة والنماء

DURR-FULL:v8p329/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the man created alone as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: الوليد بن المغيرة

DURR-FULL:v8p329/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r2.claim: Mujahid says al-Walid was created alone, without wealth or children.
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة {وحيدا} قال: خلقته وحده لا مال له ولا ولد

DURR-FULL:v8p329/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r9.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r9.claim: Abu Malik also identifies the man as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r9.anchor: عن أبي مالك {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: الوليد بن المغيرة

DURR-FULL:v8p329/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r13.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies al-Walid ibn al-Mughira ibn Hisham al-Makhzumi, father of thirteen sons, and says after the hostile verse his person, wealth, and children kept declining until his death.
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r13.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} الآيات قال: هو الوليد بن المغيرة بن هشام المخزومي وكان له ثلاثة عشر ولدا كلهم رب بيت

DURR-FULL:v8p330/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p330/r1.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p330/r1.claim: Ikrima’s report from Ibn Abbas, authenticated by al-Hakim and also transmitted mursal by Ikrima, says al-Walid softened after hearing Qurʾan; Abu Jahl pressured him for a hostile public verdict, and after reflecting he called it transmitted magic, prompting this revelation.
DURR-FULL:v8p330/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن الوليد بن المغيرة جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأ عليه القرآن فكأنه رق له فبلغ ذلك أبا جهل فأتاه

DURR-FULL:v8p330/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p330/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p330/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that al-Walid told Quraysh the Qurʾan was neither poetry, sorcery, nor madness but God’s speech; fearing he would convert others, Abu Jahl intervened and accused him of visiting Abu Bakr for food.
DURR-FULL:v8p330/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: دخل الوليد بن المغيرة على أبي بكر فسأله عن القرآن فلما أخبره خرج على قريش فقال: يا عجبا لما يقول ابن أبي كبشة

DURR-FULL:v8p331/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p331/r1.speaker: الوليد
DURR-FULL:v8p331/r1.claim: Al-Walid rejected the Qur’an as inherited magic and said he would avoid Abu Bakr, Umar, and Muhammad; this prompted the passage beginning “Leave Me with the one I created.”
DURR-FULL:v8p331/r1.anchor: فقال الوليد: تحدث بهذا عشيرتي فوالله لا أقرب ابن أبي قحافة ولا عمر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r1.claim: Mujahid says this passage was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا قال : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r2.claim: Mujahid explains that God created him alone, with no wealth or children.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r2.anchor: وحيدا قال : خلقته وحده لا مال له ولا ولد

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r9.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr identifies the man as al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra b. Hishām al-Makhzūmī and says he had thirteen sons, each a household head.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r9.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا الايات ، قال : هو الوليد بن المغيرة بن هشام المخزومي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p302/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p302/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p302/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Quraysh debated what to call Muhammad; after rejecting ‘poet,’ ‘soothsayer,’ and ‘madman,’ al-Walid chose ‘sorcerer’ because his words divided families, and this verse and following verses were revealed about him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p302/r1.anchor: ما رواه ابن إسحاق أنه اجتمع نفر من قريش فيهم أبو لهب ، وأبو سفيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r1.claim: There is agreement that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira made the statement and is the person meant by ‘the one I created alone.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r1.anchor: وقع الاتفاق على أن هذا القول صدر عن الوليد بن المغيرة وأنه المعني بقوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r2.claim: If al-Walid spoke after the sura's opening, this begins a new section; if his statement occasioned the sura, it connects to 74:7 as God's undertaking to punish him, with intervening verses parenthetical.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r2.anchor: فإن كان قول الوليد صدر منه بعد نزول صدر هذه السورة فجملة { ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا } مستأنفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r3.claim: On the strongest chronology, revelation began in Ramadan and the hiatus lasted forty days; near the end of Dhu al-Qi'da, Quraysh prepared for the approaching pilgrimage season.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r3.anchor: ويؤيد هذا أن ابتداء الوحي كان في رمضان وأن فترة الوحي دامت أربعين يوما على الأصح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r4.claim: ‘Leave Me’ implies that the Prophet was troubled by al-Walid's fabrication and makes the connection with ‘be patient for your Lord’ clearer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r4.anchor: كان مهتما ومغتما مما اختلقه الوليد بن المغيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r5.claim: The threat resembles that in 68:44, discussed in the commentary on that verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r5.anchor: وتقدم ما في نحو ذرني } وكذا ، من التهديد والوعيد للمذكور بعد واو المعية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r6.claim: The relative pronoun and clause fold al-Walid's ingratitude for God's favor into the warning and threat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r6.anchor: وجيء بالموصول وصلته في قوله : ومن خلقت وحيدا } لإدماج تسجيل كفران الوليد النعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r7.claim: Waḥīdan is an accusative circumstantial qualifier of the relative pronoun man.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r7.anchor: وانتصب { وحيدا } على الحال من { من } الموصولة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r8.claim: Waḥīd means alone in place or condition, or distinguished in fame or story, as context indicates; it derives from waḥada, ‘to be alone.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r8.anchor: والوحيد : المنفرد عن غيره في مكان أو حال مما يدل عليه سياق الكلام ،

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r9.claim: Al-Walid was nicknamed ‘the unique one’ for combining wealth, sons, family standing, and leadership among Quraysh, where he was older than Abu Jahl and Abu Sufyan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r9.anchor: وكان الوليد بن المغيرة يلقب في قريش بالوحيد لتوحده وتفرده باجتماع مزايا له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r10.claim: After ‘I created him,’ waḥīd shifts from al-Walid's boastful title to his original dependence on God, created without wealth, sons, or power, like humanity's birth without knowledge in 16:78.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p303/r10.anchor: وجاء هذا الوصف بعد فعل { خلقت ، } ليصرف هذا الوصف عما كان مرادا به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r14.claim: The transmitted referent of “leave me with the one I created alone” is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, father of Khalid ibn al-Walid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r14.anchor: الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي أبا خالد بن الوليد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r1.claim: This is a pure threat: God Himself will take care of the man's punishment and entire affair.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا وعيد محض، المعنى أنا أكفي عقابه وشأنه كله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r2.speaker: المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r2.claim: Commentators agree the passage concerns al-Walid ibn al-Mughira; a report says he was called al-Wahid for having no equal in wealth and family standing, though Ibn Atiyya says this is unproved.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r2.anchor: ولا خلاف بين المفسرين أن هذه الآية نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، فروي أنه كان يلقب الوحيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r3.claim: If the nickname report is unproved, alone means created lowly and with little, so the later wealth and sons contrast with his original state.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r3.anchor: وإن لم يثبت هذا، فقوله تعالى: خلقت وحيدا معناه منفردا قليلا ذليلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r4.claim: Another parsing takes alone to mean that God created him without a partner; وحيدا is circumstantial accusative attached to خلقت.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r4.anchor: وقيل المعنى خلقته وحدي لم يشركني فيه أحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r1.claim: The phrase “leave Me” was explained earlier at 73:11.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r2.claim: God created al-Walīd alone in his mother's womb, without wealth or children.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r2.anchor: أحدهما خلقته وحيدا في بطن أمه لا مال له ولا ولد قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r3.claim: Alternatively, God created him alone, with no partner sharing in his creation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r3.anchor: والثاني خلقته وحدي لم يشركني في خلقه أحد قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that al-Walīd heard the Prophet recite Qurʾān and nearly softened; Abū Jahl accused him of seeking the Prophet's wealth, then pressured him to denounce the recitation. Al-Walīd called it learned magic, and the verses were revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس جاء الوليد بن المغيرة إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأ عليه القرآن فكأنه رق له فبلغ ذلك أبا جهل فأتاه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r5.claim: Mujāhid recounts that al-Walīd convened Quraysh at Dār al-Nadwa to agree on a description of the Prophet; he rejected “poet,” “soothsayer,” and “madman,” settled on “sorcerer,” and Quraysh spread the charge, prompting revelation of the sūra through 74:25.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد قال الوليد لقريش إن لي إليكم حاجة فاجتمعوا في دار الندوة فقال إنكم ذوو أحساب وأحلام وإن العرب يأتونكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r6.claim: Some exegetes said this verse was abrogated by the sword verse, but Ibn al-Jawzī rejects that claim as unsound.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p403#5/r6.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن قوله تعالى ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا منسوخ بآية السيف ولا يصح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r1.claim: God threatens this wicked man, who answered worldly blessings with ingratitude, denied God’s signs, and falsely claimed they were human speech.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى متوعدا لهذا الخبيث الذي أنعم الله عليه بنعم الدنيا، فكفر بأنعم الله، وبدلها كفرا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r2.claim: He came from his mother’s womb alone, without wealth or children, and God later provided for him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r2.anchor: أي: خرج من بطن أمه وحده لا مال له ولا ولد، ثم رزقه الله

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.claim: The passage is said to concern al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, wealthy with sons and called al-Wahid among his people, according to Ibn Amir.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.anchor: قيل: نزلت هذه الآيات في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، وكان له مال وبنون، قال ابن عامر: وكان يسمى الوحيد في قومه،

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.claim: In the story, al-Walid rejects calling Muhammad a soothsayer, poet, or madman, then chooses “magician” and says the Qur’an separates families.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.anchor: ثم اختلفوا، فقيل: إنه أتى قريشا في ناديها، وقال: هذا الموسم، والناس يسألون عن محمد،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r1.claim: وحيدا may refer to God: leave Me alone with him, for I can exact vengeance on his behalf.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r1.anchor: فأنا أجزيك في الانتقام منه عن كل منتقم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r2.claim: Alternatively it describes God as sole creator, with no partner sharing in the man's creation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r2.anchor: خلقته وحدي لم يشركني في خلقه أحد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r3.claim: Alternatively it describes the man as originally alone, without wealth or children, like humanity's first creation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r3.anchor: خلقته وهو وحيد فريد لا مال له ولا ولد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r4.claim: The passage is said to concern al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, nicknamed al-Waḥīd among his people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r4.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r5.claim: His title may have arisen after the verse; if earlier, the verse mocks it by turning praise of worldly distinction into blame for being created destitute.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r5.anchor: ولعله لقب بذلك بعد نزول الآية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r6.claim: God gave him wealth and children after creating him alone, yet he repaid the blessing with disbelief, associationism, and mockery of religion.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r1.claim: The passage concerns al-Walid ibn al-Mughira; he is singled out for ingratitude and hostility toward the Messenger, though all people were created like him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r1.anchor: يعني الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي وإن كان الناس خلقوا مثل خلقه , وإنما خص بالذكر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r2.claim: One reading of wahidan is that God alone created him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r2.anchor: أحدهما : أن الله تفرد بخلقه وحده .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r3.claim: Mujahid says he was created alone in his mother's womb, with neither wealth nor children.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r3.anchor: الثاني : خلقه وحيدا في بطن أمه لا مال له ولا ولد , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r4.claim: On the second reading, his solitary creation highlights the blessings of wealth and children later given to him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r4.anchor: أن يعلم به قدر النعمةعليه فيما أعطي من المال والولد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r5.claim: On the second reading, his solitary creation also signals that he will be resurrected alone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r5.anchor: أن يدله بذلك على أنه يبعث وحيدا كما خلق وحيدا

MUQATIL:74:8-11/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r3.claim: The singularly created man is al-Walid b. al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, known as the unique one among his people.
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r3.anchor: يعني الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، كان يسمى الوحيد في قومه، وذلك أن الله

MUQATIL:74:8-11/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r4.claim: After the verses of Ghafir were revealed, Muhammad recited them in the Sacred Mosque near al-Walid, then repeated them when he noticed him listening.
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r4.anchor: فلما نزلت هذه الآية قام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في المسجد الحرام فقرأها والوليد بن المغيرة قريبا منه يستمع إلى قراءته

MUQATIL:74:8-11/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r5.claim: In the recitation, al-Aziz means sovereign in His dominion and al-Alim means knowing His creation.
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r5.anchor: { حم تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز } في ملكه { العليم } بخلقه

MUQATIL:74:8-11/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r6.claim: God forgives and accepts repentance from those who repent of associating partners with Him.
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r6.anchor: { غافر الذنب } لمن تاب من الشرك، { وقابل التوب } لمن تاب من الشرك

MUQATIL:74:8-11/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r7.claim: God severely punishes those who do not repent of shirk, and dhi al-tawl means self-sufficient from anyone who does not affirm His unity.
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r7.anchor: { شديد العقاب } لمن لم يتب من الشرك { ذي الطول } يعني ذي الغنى عمن لم يوحد،

MUQATIL:74:8-11/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r8.claim: God affirms His unity against Meccan polytheists; all creatures return to Him in the afterlife.
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r8.anchor: { لا إله إلا هو إليه المصير } يعني مصير الخلائق في الآخرة إليه

MUQATIL:74:8-11/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r9.claim: Al-Walid praised the recitation as unlike human or jinn speech, deeply rooted, elevated, sweet, beautiful, and unsurpassable.
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r9.anchor: والله، لقد سمعت من محمد كلاما آنفا ما هو من كلام الإنس، ولا من كلام الجن

MUQATIL:74:8-11/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r10.claim: Quraysh feared al-Walid's conversion would draw the whole tribe; Abu Jahl exploited that fear by claiming his praise was bought with food, which al-Walid rejected.
MUQATIL:74:8-11/r10.anchor: فقالت قريش: لقد صبأ الوليد، والله لئن صبأ لتصبون قريش كلها

MUQATIL:74:8-17/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r1.claim: Al-Walid challenged the accusations against Muhammad: he was no soothsayer, poet, or liar, and had been known as the trustworthy one before prophethood.
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r1.anchor: وكان يسمى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل النبوة الأمين، فبرأه من هذه المغالة كلها.

MUQATIL:74:8-17/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r2.claim: When Quraysh pressed him for a charge, al-Walid pondered, grimaced, and changed color before deciding to call Muhammad's message magic.
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r2.anchor: فتفكر في نفسه ما يقول عن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ثم نظر فيما يقول عنه، ثم عبس وجهه، وبسر

MUQATIL:74:8-17/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r3.claim: The account glosses basara as grimacing and scowling, then says al-Walid assigned sorcery to Muhammad.
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r3.anchor: وبسر يعني وكلح، فذلك قوله عز وجل

MUQATIL:74:8-17/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r4.claim: Al-Walid described the alleged magic as dividing families and claimed it came from Musaylima the liar; he also accused Yasar Abu Fukayha of bringing it from Musaylima.
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r4.anchor: فهذا الذي يقول محمد سحر يؤثر عن مسيلمة بن حبيب الحنفي الكذاب يقول: يرويه عنه

MUQATIL:74:8-17/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r5.claim: The false accusation distressed Muhammad especially, so God consoled him with the statement that earlier messengers were likewise called sorcerers or madmen.
MUQATIL:74:8-17/r5.anchor:
فأنزل الله تعالى على نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم
يعزيه ليصبر على تكذيبهم، فقال: يا محمد

MUQATIL:74:11-17/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:11-17/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:11-17/r1.claim: God tells Muhammad to leave Him alone with al-Walid to destroy him; He created al-Walid initially without wealth or sons, then gave him both.
MUQATIL:74:11-17/r1.anchor: { ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا } يقول: خل بينى يا محمد وبين من خلقت وحيدا، يقول: حين لم يكن له مال ولا بنون

NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r1.claim: The man is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, known among his people as “the one and only”.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r1.anchor: إلى عيني الوليد بن المغيرة وكان يلقب في قومه بالوحيد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r2.claim: “ومن خلقت” may be coordinated with the preceding object or construed as a comitative object.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r2.anchor: ومن خلقت معطوف أو مفعول معه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r3.claim: “وحيدا” may be circumstantial from the yāʾ in “ذرني”, the tāʾ in “خلقت”, a deleted pronoun, or “من”.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r3.anchor: ﴿ وحيدا ﴾ حال من الياء في ذرني

NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r4.claim: If it describes the yāʾ in “ذرني”, God says to leave him alone with Me, for God will handle him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r4.anchor: أي اترني وحدي معه فإني أكفيك أمره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r5.claim: If it describes the tāʾ in “خلقت”, God created him alone without a partner, family, or wealth before blessing him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p294#10/r5.anchor: أي خلقته وحدي لم يشركني في خلقه أحدا ومن الهاء المحذوفة أو من أي خلقته منفردا بلا أهل ولا مال ثم انعمت عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r1.claim: “Leave me” is a threat and warning.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r1.anchor: ذرني } أي دعني وهي كلمة وعيد وتهديد

QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r2.claim: On the ordinary reading, wahidan is circumstantial for the omitted object: God created him alone, with no wealth or children, then bestowed gifts.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r2.anchor: ف «وحيدا» على هذا حال من ضمير المفعول المحذوف، أي خلقته وحده

QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r3.claim: The commentators identify the man as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, singled out for ingratitude and harming the Messenger.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r3.anchor: والمفسرون على أنه الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي

QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-Walid boasted he was the unique son of a unique father, with no Arab equal; God repeats the boast without endorsing it.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان الوليد يقول: أنا الوحيد بن الوحيد

QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r5.claim: Mujahid takes the phrase as God’s challenge to deal with al-Walid alone, sufficient to avenge him.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r5.anchor: أحدهما: ذرني وحدي معه فأنا أجزيك في الانتقام منه

QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r6.claim: Another reading makes wahidan describe God as sole creator, able to destroy al-Walid without a helper.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r6.anchor: والثاني: أني انفردت بخلقه ولم يشركني فيه أحد، فأنا أهلكه

QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r7.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r7.claim: Mujahid says al-Walid began alone in his mother’s womb, without wealth or child, before God enriched him.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r7.anchor: والأول قول مجاهد، أي خلقته وحيدا في بطن أمه لا مال له

QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r8.claim: Another interpretation says he will be resurrected alone just as created alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r8.anchor: وقيل: أراد بذلك ليدله على أنه يبعث وحيدا كما خلق وحيدا

QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r9.claim: Another gloss calls al-Walid one without a known father; Qurtubi links it to his description in 68:13.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r9.anchor: وقيل: الوحيد الذي لا يعرف أبوه، وكان الوليد معروفا بأنه دعي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r7.claim: Qatada says al-Walid was born alone from his mother.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r7.anchor: قال قتادة: خرج من بطن أمه وحيدا

TAB-FULL:v23p428/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r3.claim: Ikrima recounts that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira was moved by Muhammad's recitation and praised its sweetness and force, but after Abu Jahl pressured him to oppose it he decided to call it magic inherited from another; the passage was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة أن الوليد بن المغيرة جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقرأ عليه القرآن، فكأنه رق له

TAB-FULL:v23p428/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r4.claim: Qatada says al-Walid was created alone from his mother's womb and that the revelation then ran through the verse about nineteen.
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: خرج من بطن أمه وحيدا، فنزلت هذه الآية حتى بلغ {تسعة عشر} [المدثر: 30]

TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the solitary one as al-Walid, whom Muhammad invited to Islam; after delaying, considering, frowning, turning away, and calling the message magic, he was consigned to Saqar.
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} [المدثر: 11] يعني الوليد بن المغيرة دعاه نبي الله

TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts that al-Walid examined Muhammad reciting in prayer, called the speech sweet and heart-gripping, rejected poetry and soothsaying, then allowed that it might be magic transmitted from earlier people.
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا وجعلت له مالا ممدودا} [المدثر: 12] إلى قوله

FARRA:v3p200/r13.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p200/r13.speaker: بعضهم
FARRA:v3p200/r13.claim: One view takes وحيدا to mean that God created him alone.
FARRA:v3p200/r13.anchor: [الوحيد ] فيه وجهان، قال بعضهم: ذرني ومن خلقته وحدي،

FARRA:v3p200/r14.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p200/r14.speaker: آخرون
FARRA:v3p200/r14.claim: Others take it to mean he was created alone, without wealth or sons; al-Farra says this is the more comprehensive of the two views.
FARRA:v3p200/r14.anchor: وقال آخرون: خلقته وحده لا مال له ولا بنين، وهو أجمع الوجهين.

FARRA:v3p200/r19.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p200/r19.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p200/r19.claim: The “solitary” is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p446/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p446/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p446/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that al-Walid heard the Quran and praised its sweet, forceful language as unlike poetry, but after Abu Jahl pressed him to denounce Muhammad he called it transmitted magic; verses 74:11–24 were revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p446/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أن الوليد بن المغيرة جاء إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقرأ عليه القرآن وكأنه رق له، فبلغ ذلك أبا جهل،
